speaker: Doctor
text: The blisters are described as flaccid and rupture easily, leaving painful erosions, while the mucosal ulcers appeared shortly after starting captopril. Given the history of autoimmune conditions and the specific presentation of flaccid bullae with mucosal involvement, I suspect an autoimmune blistering disease. REQUEST TEST: Direct_Immunofluorescence and REQUEST IMAGES.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Direct Immunofluorescence shows intercellular IgG and C3 deposition within the epidermis. Skin biopsy histopathology reveals acantholysis and intraepidermal blister formation. Blood tests confirm the presence of desmoglein antibodies. Vital signs are stable with Temperature 36.8°C, Blood Pressure 130/85 mmHg, Heart Rate 72 bpm, and Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min. Physical exam confirms multiple flaccid blisters on the forearm (10% TBSA), a positive Nikolsky sign, and ulcers on buccal, gingival, and vulvar mucosa.

speaker: Doctor
text: The test results confirm a diagnosis of Pemphigus Vulgaris, an autoimmune blistering disease triggered by your new captopril medication. We will immediately discontinue the captopril and begin treatment with systemic corticosteroids and supportive wound care. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pemphigus Vulgaris
